title: SAT Math Strategies, Reference Sheet, and Desmos
subtitle: Choose efficient representations, use the reference sheet strategically, and make Desmos work for you.

isi.content: Strong SAT Math performance is not only about knowing formulas. It also depends on deciding what the question asks, selecting a useful representation, estimating before calculating, and checking whether the result makes sense.

items: Focus on the goal: identify the exact quantity, expression, or statement requested.
Choose a representation: use an equation, sketch, table, graph, easy numbers, formula, or calculator.
Estimate or eliminate: predict the sign, size, units, and possible domain before doing all the work.
Calculate and verify: check the result against the original conditions.

isi.content: A strategy should make correct mathematics faster and clearer. It should never replace careful reading of the question.
Read the final sentence carefully. Many SAT questions provide more information than you need. If the question asks for an expression, you may not need to find every variable separately.

isi.title: Example: calculate only the requested expression
isi.content: If \(4x+2=12\), then \(4x=10\). Therefore, \(16x+8=4(4x)+8=4(10)+8=48\). The requested expression can be found without first solving for \(x\).

items.title: Target
items.content: What number, expression, graph feature, or statement must be reported?

items.title: Relevant details
items.content: Which values and conditions actually affect that target?

items.title: Verification
items.content: Does the result have the correct sign, size, units, and domain?

isi.content: A quick sketch can organize lengths, angles, areas, and relationships. The drawing does not need to be perfectly scaled; it only needs to label the important quantities.

isi.title: Example: rectangle and diagonal
isi.content: A rectangle has area 540 square feet and length 36 feet. Its width is \(w=540\div36=15\) feet. If the diagonal is needed, use the Pythagorean theorem: \(d=\sqrt{36^2+15^2}=\sqrt{1521}=39\) feet.

items: Label known lengths and unknown lengths.
Mark a right angle when the Pythagorean theorem or right-triangle trigonometry may apply.
Separate area, perimeter, surface area, and volume.
Write units beside measurements so the requested unit stays visible.

isi.content: Before calculating, identify details that control the answer: signs, units, restrictions, definitions, and boundary words. Ignore decorative information that does not affect the target.

items.title: Sign
items.content: An absolute value cannot be negative, and a length or probability cannot be negative.

items.title: Size
items.content: A percentage between 0% and 100% cannot be represented by a value such as 250% unless the context allows it.

items.title: Units
items.content: Area uses square units, volume uses cubic units, and rates must be multiplied by compatible units.

items.title: Domain
items.content: Check restrictions such as a positive denominator, a nonnegative radicand, or a whole-number count.

isi.title: Example: eliminate by sign
isi.content: Because \(\left|f(x)\right|\ge0\), any negative answer for the value of \(\left|f(x)\right|\) choice can be eliminated before substituting values.
When a problem describes a percentage or ratio but does not give a total, choose a convenient total. The number 100 is especially useful because percentages become whole numbers.

isi.title: Example: two consecutive percentages
isi.content:
If 40% of students have blue eyes and 20% of those students have brown hair, what percent of the original group has both characteristics?

Imagine 100 students. If 40% have blue eyes, 40 students have blue eyes. If 20% of those students have brown hair, then \(0.20(40)=8\) students have both characteristics. Thus, 8% of the original group has both.
You may choose any convenient total that preserves the relationships. The answer should not depend on the particular total you choose.
\[\text{percent change}=\frac{\text{new}-\text{original}}{\text{original}}\times100\%\]
The original amount is the reference for a percent change. A percent increase or decrease can also be modeled with a multiplier.

isi.title: Example: sequential changes
isi.content: A 15% increase followed by another 15% increase gives \(\text{final}=\text{original}(1.15)(1.15)=1.3225(\text{original})\). The total increase is 32.25%, not 30%, because the second increase is based on the new amount.
\[\text{mean}=\frac{\text{sum of the values}}{\text{number of values}}\]

items: Adding the same number to every data value adds that number to the mean and leaves the standard deviation unchanged.
Multiplying every data value by a positive number \(k\) multiplies both the mean and the standard deviation by \(k\).
When finding a missing data value, first calculate the required total from the mean.

isi.content: The SAT reference sheet can save time, but only when you recognize the shape or relationship in the problem. Identify what each variable represents before substituting.

isi.title: Example: cylinder volume
isi.content: A cylinder has radius 2 inches and height 8 inches. Using \(V=\pi r^2h\), the volume is \(\pi(2)^2(8)=32\pi\) cubic inches.
For an equilateral triangle with side length \(s\), the height is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\). This relationship can be derived by splitting the triangle into two 30-60-90 triangles.
Desmos is useful for graphing equations and inequalities, finding intersections, checking zeros and intercepts, building tables, and evaluating expressions involving exponents or radicals.

items: Enter each equation on its own line.
Use parentheses carefully, especially around negative numbers and exponents.
Click an intersection point to read its coordinates.
Use a table when a question asks for repeated values or a pattern.
Use the graph to identify a zero, intercept, maximum, minimum, or solution region.
Check that the displayed value matches the requested units and rounding.

isi.title: Example: find an intersection
isi.content: For \(y=3x-5\) and \(y=-x+11\), set the expressions equal: \(3x-5=-x+11\), so \(x=4\), and then \(y=7\). Desmos can display the intersection \((4,7)\), while substitution verifies it.

isi.title: Example: identify when an exponential doubles
isi.content: For \(f(t)=40{,}000(2)^{t/790}\), doubling occurs when the exponent is 1. Thus, \(t/790=1\), so \(t=790\) minutes.
Use mental math for a simple one-step calculation. Use Desmos when graphing, repeated evaluation, nonlinear behavior, or verification makes the tool genuinely useful.

items: Estimate before calculating so an implausible answer is easier to notice.
Use answer choices as information; substitution can be faster than solving symbolically.
Keep units visible in intermediate work.
If a question is taking too long, mark it, move on, and return after securing easier points.
Before moving on, ask whether the answer matches the question's requested form: integer, fraction, percentage, coordinate, or unit.

latihan.question: If \(4x+2=12\), what is the value of \(16x+8\)?
discussion: From \(4x+2=12\), subtract 2 to get \(4x=10\).
Rewrite the target as \(16x+8=4(4x)+8\).
Therefore, \(16x+8=4(10)+8=48\). The correct answer is B.

latihan.question: Given \(x+1=\dfrac{2}{x+1}\), which is a possible value of \(x+1\)?
discussion: Thus, \(u=\sqrt2\) or \(u=-\sqrt2\).
Among the choices, \(\sqrt2\) is possible, so the correct answer is B.

latihan.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(\dfrac{8x(x-7)-3(x-7)}{2x-14}\), where \(x>7\)?
discussion: Factor the numerator: \(8x(x-7)-3(x-7)=(x-7)(8x-3)\).
Factor the denominator: \(2x-14=2(x-7)\).
Since \(x>7\), \(x-7\ne0\), so the expression simplifies to \(\dfrac{8x-3}{2}\).

latihan.question: An event planner pays a one-time venue fee of USD \(35\) and USD \(10.25\) per attendee. With a USD \(300\) budget, what is the greatest possible whole-number of attendees?
discussion: Let \(n\) be the number of attendees. The cost model is \(35+10.25n\le300\).
Divide by 10.25: \(n\le25.8536\ldots\).
Because attendees are counted in whole numbers, the greatest possible value is \(25\).

latihan.question: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 624 centimeters. Its height is \(k\sqrt3\) centimeters. Find \(k\).
discussion: Each side has length \(624\div3=208\) centimeters.
The height of an equilateral triangle is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\).
Therefore, the height is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}(208)=104\sqrt3\), so \(k=104\).

latihan.question: A machine produces beads, and 29 out of every 100 beads are defective. What is the probability of selecting a defective bead?
discussion: The phrase “29 out of every 100” directly represents the ratio \(\dfrac{29}{100}\).
This ratio is already a valid probability between 0 and 1.
The correct answer is C.

latihan.question: Given \(\dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}=\dfrac{c^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}+39\), where \(c\) is positive, which is one solution?
discussion: Subtract the two fractions and multiply by the positive denominator: \(x^2-c^2=39\sqrt{x^2-c^2}\).
Let \(u=\sqrt{x^2-c^2}\). Then \(u^2=39u\), and because the denominator is defined, \(u>0\), so \(u=39\).
The negative solution is \(x=-\sqrt{c^2+39^2}\), choice D.

latihan.question: Given \(b=3\) and \(d=1\), which is equivalent to \(\left|\dfrac{2b-3}{-4d+1}\right|\)?
discussion: Substitute \(b=3\) and \(d=1\): \(\left|\dfrac{2(3)-3}{-4(1)+1}\right|=\left|\dfrac{3}{-3}\right|\).
The absolute value of \(-1\) is 1.
The correct answer is D. The sign check also eliminates negative choices.

latihan.question: If \(f(x)=(x+6)(x+5)(x-4)\), which table represents \(y=f(x)-3\)?
discussion: At \(x=-6,-5,4\), one factor of \(f(x)\) is zero, so \(f(x)=0\).
Therefore, \(y=f(x)-3=-3\) at all three inputs.
The correct table is choice B.

latihan.question: If \(x\) represents an even integer, which expression represents an odd integer?
discussion: Any multiple of an even integer is even.
The expression \(2x\) is even, and adding 1 makes it odd.
Thus, \(2x+1\) is always odd, choice B.

latihan.question: Solve \(\sqrt{2x+6}+4=x+3\).
discussion: Isolate the radical: \(\sqrt{2x+6}=x-1\), so the right side requires \(x\ge1\).
Square both sides: \(2x+6=(x-1)^2=x^2-2x+1\).
The domain excludes \(-1\), and checking \(x=5\) works. The answer is B.

latihan.question: The base of triangle \(T\) is 40% less than the length of rectangle \(R\). The height of triangle \(T\) is 50% greater than the width of rectangle \(R\). The area of \(T\) is what percent of the area of \(R\)?
discussion: Let the rectangle's length and width be \(L\) and \(W\).
The triangle's base is \(0.60L\), and its height is \(1.50W\).
Since \(A_R=LW\), the triangle's area is 45% of the rectangle's area.

latihan.question: If 40% of students have blue eyes and 20% of those students have brown hair, what percent of the original group has both characteristics?
discussion: Imagine 100 students. Then 40 students have blue eyes.
Twenty percent of those 40 students is \(0.20(40)=8\).
Therefore, 8 out of 100 students, or 8%, have both characteristics.

latihan.question: A graduated cylinder has radius 2 inches and height 7.75 inches. What is its volume, rounded to the nearest cubic inch?
discussion: Use the cylinder formula \(V=\pi r^2h\).
Since \(31\pi\approx97.39\), the volume rounds to 97 cubic inches.

latihan.question: Given \(y=-(x-3)^2+a\), which statement is true?
discussion: The vertex form is \(y=A(x-h)^2+k\), with vertex \((h,k)\).
Here, the vertex is \((3,a)\).
Because the coefficient of the squared term is negative, the parabola opens downward and the vertex is a maximum. Choice D is correct.

latihan.question: The function \(f(t)=40{,}000(2)^{t/790}\) gives the number of bacteria \(t\) minutes after observation. How many minutes does it take to double?
discussion: The initial population is 40,000. To double it, the exponential factor must be 2.
Therefore, \(t=790\) minutes, choice B.

latihan.question: What is the mean of \(25,28,23,36,29\)?
discussion: There are 5 values, so the mean is \(141\div5=28.2\).

additionalPractice.question: If \(7x=42\), what is \(x\)?
discussion: Divide both sides by 7: \(x=42\div7=6\).
The correct answer is B.

additionalPractice.question: What is the mean of \(8,10,12,14\)?
discussion: There are 4 values, so the mean is \(44\div4=11\).

additionalPractice.question: What is 25% of 80?
discussion: Convert 25% to 0.25 and multiply: \(0.25(80)=20\).
The correct answer is B.

additionalPractice.question: A quantity increases from 120 to 150. What is the percentage increase?
discussion: The increase is \(150-120=30\).
Use the original amount as the denominator: \(\dfrac{30}{120}\times100\%=25\%\).
The correct answer is B.

additionalPractice.question: The mean of five numbers is 18. Four numbers are 12, 15, 20, and 21. What is the fifth number?
discussion: The total of all five values must be \(5(18)=90\).
The four known values sum to \(12+15+20+21=68\).
The missing value is \(90-68=22\), choice C.

additionalPractice.question: A rectangle has area 180 square units and length 15 units. What is its perimeter?
discussion: The width is \(180\div15=12\) units.
The perimeter is \(2(15+12)=54\) units.
The correct answer is B.

additionalPractice.question: A rectangle has length 20% greater than its width. Its area is 270 square units. What is its perimeter?
discussion: Let the width be \(w\). Then the length is \(1.2w\).
The area equation is \(1.2w^2=270\), so \(w^2=225\) and \(w=15\).
The length is \(1.2(15)=18\), so the perimeter is \(2(15+18)=66\).

additionalPractice.question: A data set has mean 40 and standard deviation 6. Each data value is multiplied by 3. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
discussion: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the mean by 3: \(40(3)=120\).
It also multiplies the standard deviation by 3: \(6(3)=18\).
The correct answer is B.

additionalPractice.question: A quantity is increased by 15% and then increased by another 15%. What is the total percent increase?
discussion: Two consecutive 15% increases give the multiplier \((1.15)(1.15)=1.3225\).
The final value is 1.3225 times the original, which represents a 32.25% increase.
The correct answer is C.
